title: Per-route lightweight sampling heuristics to minimize tracing hot-path overhead
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Tracing instrumentation throughout the serving runtime continues to add measurable CPU and allocation overhead on very hot request paths. We have several large-scale sampling efforts (tail-based, reservoir, adaptive) but they either live off-hotpath or still require per-request work that increases p50 under peak QPS. Goal: Introduce a per-route, heuristic-driven sampling decision that runs in O(1) and uses only lightweight local counters and probabilistic bucketing to make sampling decisions fully on the hot path with negligible allocation and lock contention. This ticket covers design, implementation, benchmarking, rollout, and safety gates (perf regression detection and automatic fallback).

Acceptance criteria:
- Hot-path sampling decision reduces allocations and CPU work for tracing by >= 60% versus current adaptive sampler at 95th percentile for the /generate and /embed routes, measured on benchmark rigs representative of production (A100/RTX).
- No more than 2% increase in tail latency (99.9th) across target routes during canary at 50% traffic.
- Configurable per-route policy exposed in runtime config and Redwood Console (can be toggled without restart).
- Graceful fallback to current reservoir/tail samplers when memory/metric signals exceed safe thresholds or when the new sampler reports errors.

Technical approach summary:
1) Instrument a compact per-route sampling state: a single 64-bit atomic that encodes a token bucket-ish counter and a tiny random seed. Avoid maps on hot path by indexing routes by ID.
2) Decision logic: decrement-only counter with probabilistic sampling when counter <= 0. Use xorshift64 for cheap RNG and bitmask to decide sample vs skip. No heap allocations; no mutexes.
3) Background controller: periodically (1s) aggregates lightweight metrics (sampled count, seen count, queue backlog) and adjusts route counters/thresholds using a PID-like controller. Controller runs off-hotpath.
4) Safety guard: integrate with tracing health signals and console alerts. If the controller observes sudden drop in sample quality (measured vs ground-truth shadow sampling for a small percentage of traffic) or resource pressure (latency increases or allocation spikes), flip a runtime flag to route traffic back to the legacy sampler automatically.
5) Opt-in per-route config: expose policy via runtime config and Console; defaults for high-throughput routes will be enabled behind a kill-switch.

Metrics to collect (added to runtime metrics):
- sampler.hotpath.allocs_delta (gauge delta vs baseline),
- sampler.hotpath.cpu_ns (cumulative CPU ns consumed),
- sampler.sample_rate_per_route (gauge),
- sampler.fallback_count (counter),
- sampler.shadow_agreement_ratio (gauge)

Rollout plan:
- Dev bench + unit tests (this ticket) -> branch perf bench and microbench PR.
- Canary on staging with 1% traffic and shadow sampling enabled for 24h. Monitor shadow_agreement_ratio >= 0.95.
- Gradual ramp to 50% over 48h with automated rollback on SLO breaches.
- Full rollout after two successful cycles and infra sign-off.

Rollback criteria:
- Any single canary region shows >2% increase in 99.9th latency for target routes, or
- sampler.shadow_agreement_ratio drops below 0.9 for 30m, or
- fallback_count exceeds configured threshold, or
- increase in allocation rate that correlates with sampler changes.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Triage: Discussed with Observability subgroup. Riley Chen suggested encoding route id + counters in a single atomic to avoid maps. Assigned to Miguel.

2026-03-03 — Design review: Presented architecture to runtime and infra. Action items: add shadow sampling bridge for validation (Riley), create perf microbench harness (Samir), and list required metrics for Console (PM owner: Lina Kaur).

2026-03-05 — Implementation started: added route ID indexing and xorshift64 RNG skeleton. Microbench harness reproduces p50/p95 on synthetic traffic. Initial microbench shows ~40% reduction in sampler allocations on hotpath for /embed route.

2026-03-07 — Perf tuning: Adjusted controller tick from 500ms to 1s to reduce off-path CPU. Also optimized RNG bitmask to avoid modulus. Bench shows further reduction in CPU cycles, now ~58% allocation reduction vs legacy adaptive sampler under 95th percentile load.

2026-03-08 — PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9821 (WIP). Included unit tests for atomic packing and a synthetic workload test. Requesting review from backend-runtime and instrumentation owners.

2026-03-09 — Review notes from backend-runtime: ask to add a metrics tag for route_version, ensure no behavior change for cold-started routes, and include feature-flag gating via config-service (Miguel to follow up).
2026-03-10 — Added shadow-sampler bridge: runs legacy sampler in background for 0.1% of traffic to compute ground-truth agreement. Initial agreement: 0.962 on synthetic bench.
2026-03-10 — Next: finalize Console toggle design with PM, draft canary runbook, and schedule staging canary for 2026-03-13.
